key_insight: Small language models can learn abstract reasoning rules, but their success is highly sensitive to model family, training setup, and evaluation distribution.
engineering_relevance: For robust deployment, abstract-reasoning evaluation must test transfer, scale shifts, and response formats—not just in-distribution accuracy.
method: Studied decoder-only, encoder--decoder, and mixture-of-experts models on ARC-TGI under supervised fine-tuning.
Ran more than 1,000 experiments to compare learning stability, robustness, task-family effects, and attention signatures.
Tested cross-benchmark transfer, spatial shifts, resampling, and executable-rule induction versus direct grid generation.
evidence_signal: Across over 1,000 runs on ARC-TGI, models achieved strong in-distribution accuracy but often failed under distribution shifts, including changed grid scale.
watch_item: Attention patterns may correlate with behavior, but the paper does not establish that they are causal mechanisms for abstract reasoning.
paper_title: A Systematic Study of Small Language Models on Abstract Reasoning Tasks
